response.reason: NL1 is purely descriptive/introductory context with no independently violable obligation. NL2 establishes a continuous operating task (target search) prior to mission completion, plus a cardinality/structure obligation of three state areas (region_structure/cardinality, domain unresolved between concurrent_regions and direct_child_states since 'state areas' is generic and no explicit parallelism is stated, but no clear count-domain conflict since NL explicitly gives count=3). NL3 establishes a transition endpoint from the ongoing swarm operating state to formation adjustment, triggered by an interception event. NL4 establishes an initial-entry-like transition (task assignment reception triggers entry to attack state) and a separate variable-delta effect (UAV count decreases after completing attack), plus termination-adjacent completion of attack. I preserve these as distinct atomic contracts with typed hints, transition groups for shared sources, and mark all four segments covered.

response.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, structure, and cross-view identity contrast for the UAV swarm state machine (case 0036). Author source declares two independent orthogonal regions (Region1: TargetSearch/FormationAdjustment; Region2: AttackReady/Attack) plus a separate standalone InitialState, all directly under the implicit root state. The closed FCSTM mirrors this exact structure: three top-level children of the root (Region1, Region2, InitialState), each an independent composite/leaf, with no edge from InitialState (or root) into Region1 or Region2. Root's only outgoing edge targets InitialState, which is a leaf with zero outgoing transitions. This exposes a structural default-entry/ownership gap: the root composite that must eventually own/reach Region1 and Region2 (the loci of every downstream contract) has no edge realizing that ownership, and InitialState itself is a dead end. NL2's initial_entry contract already targets the root->target-search-state obligation; the additional gap here is that Region1 and Region2, which own the cardinality/endpoint/consumer obligations, are never entered by any default/owner-local edge from the true root, distinct from the already-covered NL2 initial-entry claim (which names the target-search state itself as target). I bind exact endpoint refs from the closed inventory/inspection-equivalent facts for every candidate and keep predicate selection to the minimal frozen ID that decides each property, using S2 for the missing/absent required edges, and predicate-null W1 where no frozen ID represents the semantic value (effect, event-consumer coverage as reachable-coverage, containment, deadlock progress with only a leaf-without-outgoing structural fact for InitialState which is compiler-owned synthetic-like placeholder but here is an authored top-level element, not synthetic).

arguments.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, structure, and cross-view identity contrast for the UAV swarm state machine (case 0036). Author source declares two independent orthogonal regions (Region1: TargetSearch/FormationAdjustment; Region2: AttackReady/Attack) plus a separate standalone InitialState, all directly under the implicit root state. The closed FCSTM mirrors this exact structure: three top-level children of the root (Region1, Region2, InitialState), each an independent composite/leaf, with no edge from InitialState (or root) into Region1 or Region2. Root's only outgoing edge targets InitialState, which is a leaf with zero outgoing transitions. This exposes a structural default-entry/ownership gap: the root composite that must eventually own/reach Region1 and Region2 (the loci of every downstream contract) has no edge realizing that ownership, and InitialState itself is a dead end. NL2's initial_entry contract already targets the root->target-search-state obligation; the additional gap here is that Region1 and Region2, which own the cardinality/endpoint/consumer obligations, are never entered by any default/owner-local edge from the true root, distinct from the already-covered NL2 initial-entry claim (which names the target-search state itself as target). I bind exact endpoint refs from the closed inventory/inspection-equivalent facts for every candidate and keep predicate selection to the minimal frozen ID that decides each property, using S2 for the missing/absent required edges, and predicate-null W1 where no frozen ID represents the semantic value (effect, event-consumer coverage as reachable-coverage, containment, deadlock progress with only a leaf-without-outgoing structural fact for InitialState which is compiler-owned synthetic-like placeholder but here is an authored top-level element, not synthetic).

Behavior-consequence obligations (state_action progress, endpoint existence under a reachable source, event-consumer coverage, and deadlock freedom) must all be assessed against this root-reachability failure and the terminal leaf. I derive one exact reachability contract for the required Region1/Region2 operating scopes and preserve one V1 deadlock candidate for the terminal InitialState leaf, plus event-consumer-coverage candidates for both required event responses (NL3 interception, NL4 task-assignment), and preserve state_action, endpoint, and deadlock-freedom candidates that are semantically defeated by the same root-unreachability cause. decisions.basis: exact_source_inventory tr_0001/tr_0002; inspection_equivalent_facts transitions and diagnostics; verify_facts reachability refuted; S2 receipt verdict=false
decisions.reason: The S2 predicate (transition_exists, source=[*], target=TargetSearch, scope=root) is refuted by the receipt (verdict=false). The exact inventory confirms the only root initial edge is tr_0001 -> InitialState, a disconnected leaf; TargetSearch is only reachable via Region1's own local initial edge tr_0002, which is never entered from root per verify_facts refuted reachability. This is a precise owner-target mismatch. The dossier itself raises a competent alternative reading (Region1's internal initial edge to TargetSearch is well-formed, and one could read the obligation as partly satisfied if Region1 is presumed pre-activated) that S2 alone does not fully exclude, leaving a genuine second reading, though the dominant reading is that root must actually reach the target.
decisions.violated_obligation: The UAV swarm root scope's initial/default entry must reach the target-search operating state (TargetSearch inside Region1).

decisions.basis: exact_source_inventory states/transitions; inspection_equivalent_facts reachable_from_initial=false; verify_facts refuted reachability check
decisions.reason: The exact transition inventory (tr_0001..tr_0007) contains no edge targeting Region1 from root; inspection_equivalent_facts marks Region1 reachable_from_initial=false and verify_facts refutes reachability. The predicate plan is unsupported (no frozen predicate id resolved), a W-boundary issue, not a defeater of the underlying fact. The dossier raises a competent alternative reading: PlantUML orthogonal-region syntax could imply simultaneous activation of sibling top-level states without an explicit entry edge, a second interpretive possibility not fully excluded by the closed FCSTM's own representation, though the closed model's semantics disfavor it.
decisions.violated_obligation: The root UAV swarm scope must have a default/initial entry edge reaching Region1 so the target-search operating region is enterable.

decisions.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic; verify_facts deadlock check refuted with outgoing_count=0; NL4 continuation requirement
decisions.reason: InitialState is confirmed by inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostic LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING and verify_facts deadlock check (refuted, outgoing_count=0) to be a reachable, non-final leaf with zero outgoing transitions, matching the V1 frontier protocol's deadlock/no-progress certificate class. The proposed intentional-terminal alternative is not supported by any exact NL terminal clause, formal terminal edge, or explicit terminal fact; NL4 explicitly requires continuation into flight/attack response, an explicit progress contract that excludes this reading, so the rebuttal is defeated.
decisions.violated_obligation: The UAV swarm's operating state during flight must remain able to respond to and progress upon receiving task assignment information rather than becoming a dead end.

decisions.basis: fcstm_model model_ir; inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostics; verify_facts refuted reachability check

decisions.violated_obligation: Region1, the composite owning TargetSearch/FormationAdjustment, must be reachable from the root.

issues.observed: Region2 is declared as a sibling composite under the root alongside InitialState, but the root's only reachable outgoing edge is [*] -> InitialState; Region2 has no incoming root-level edge and is flagged STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL, with verify_facts refuting its reachability.
issues.reason: The complete finite closed transition inventory contains no root-level edge into Region2, matching the complete-inventory absence protocol; two independent deterministic sources (inspection diagnostics and verify_facts refuted reachability check) confirm the negative fact.
issues.requirement_quote: During flight, if task assignment information is received, it enters the attack state. After completing the attack, the number of UAVs in the swarm decreases accordingly.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Region2 has a valid local initial edge ([*] -> AttackReady at transition:line:16), proved in verify_facts (initial-entry:transition:line:16); this shows Region2's internal entry is well-formed, but it does not connect Region2 to the global root, so root reachability still fails independently of this local entry fact.
issues.title: Region2 (flight/attack operating scope) is unreachable from the model root

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts event_consumers row for Interception_Detected showing reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for Interception_Detected; verify_facts check event-consumer:Interception_Detected status=refuted.
issues.expected: The interception event must be consumed by the UAV swarm's ongoing operating scope regardless of which of the three state areas it is currently in.
issues.observed: Because Region1 (owning TargetSearch/FormationAdjustment) is entirely unreachable from root, there is no reachable state area in which the interception event could ever be consumed; reachable_consumer_transition_refs for Interception_Detected is empty in inspection_equivalent_facts and the verify_facts event-consumer check is refuted.
issues.reason: This derived contract explicitly requires coverage across all three state areas, and the same deterministic non-reachability of the consumer set applies; the underlying cause is the Region1 root-unreachability defect captured separately, but the event-consumer-coverage property itself remains an independent typed obligation that must receive its own candidate per frontier discipline.
issues.requirement_quote: When the UAV swarm is intercepted, it transitions to the formation adjustment state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: This duplicates NL-CONTRACT-REF-008's event-consumer-coverage finding for the same event/consumer set; both contracts describe the identical underlying fact from slightly different NL segments (NL3 direct vs. NL3-derived all-areas framing), so the same evidence supports both but they remain formally distinct contract IDs per the sparse-response rule.
issues.title: Interception event coverage across all three state areas fails because the entire owning scope is unreachable
